audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere — it gave Tryndamere levels 2-3, which is exactly the window Nautilus's own page (already audited) claims, and the page's whys[3] already said levels 4-5 tilt to Nautilus while the chart said Skill.
audit.why: The mirror set Skill, Nautilus x5, Tryndamere. Dredge Line throws 1150 against a 650-range unit-targeted dash Tryndamere does not have until 3, and hook into Staggering Blow root into Riptide is a real level-3 all-in. Tryndamere's genuine ownership is the two-item side lane.
audit.corrected: Skill, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Tryndamere with ratings 5,4,3,3,4,4,7, proposed as matched pairs across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treated level 6 as the moment the matchup flips to Tryndamere.
audit.why: Undying Rage (120/100/80s) makes you unkillable for its window, but it does not stop Depth Charge from knocking you up and starting the fight — Nautilus still chooses the timing. The real Tryndamere spike is two items in the side lane, once he can decline the fights Nautilus starts.
audit.corrected: Level 6 reframed as survival rather than a flip; the flip moved to 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] was titled 'Eat his passive root chain' but its body was boilerplate about wasting a cooldown, and Mocking Shout's condition was never stated.
audit.why: Staggering Blow roots on Nautilus's first attack against a target — that root is what makes the rest of the chain connect. Mocking Shout (850 range, 14s) cuts his Attack Damage but only slows enemies whose backs are turned, so walking at him keeps the slow live while turning to run does not, and it hands the 1150-range hook a still target.
audit.corrected: Both written into dontsFull[1].d and dosFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that Dredge Line colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus to it, so he can cut off a retreat you have no dash to answer.
audit.why: listed in missingInteractions; Riot's text confirms the terrain pull.
audit.corrected: Recorded in notes — no existing field had room inside the band without dropping a more load-bearing fact.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Dredge Line throws 1150 and you have no dash until 3 — hug the minions so the hook has a body to hit first.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His level-3 all-in is real: hook, Staggering Blow root, then Riptide on 7s. Spinning Slash is 650 — you cannot outrange him.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Trade only after Dredge Line misses; on 14/13/12/11/10s that gap is long, and Riptide's slow keeps you parked inside Titan's Wrath.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage buys you 5 seconds, but Depth Charge still knocks you up and starts the fight on his terms — hold R for the chain, never for chip damage.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Dredge Line's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker is your spike, but he still opens — force fights only once Dredge Line has whiffed.

edits.before: Build 100 fury on the wave, E-spin onto Nautilus with a crit loaded, AA-W slow, and spin out before the answer.
edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows him while his back is turned, so walk at him — turning to run hands the hook a still target.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack — that root is what lands the chain.

edits.before: Level 2 is skill-based as you dodge Q and he sets up his engage.
edits.after: Level 2 is his — Dredge Line reaches 1150 and you have no dash yet.

edits.before: Level 3 is a skill window — his all-in is real but only if his hook lands.
edits.after: Level 3 is his — hook into passive root and Titan's Wrath is a real all-in.

edits.before: At 6 your R survives his CC chain, flipping the all-in in your favour.
edits.after: At 6 R survives his CC chain, but Depth Charge still picks when you fight.

edits.before: With your first crit item you out-scale and out-duel a support-item Nautilus.
edits.after: At first item you close the gap, but his CC chain still opens every fight.

edits.before: R Undying Rage flips the matchup — his hook combo can no longer burst you through the immortality window, so you can bait his Q, pop R if it lands, and Q Bloodlust back to full. Play for this: once you have R, his CC just delays a fight you win.
edits.after: R Undying Rage answers his burst — the hook combo cannot kill through the window, so bait Q, pop R once it lands, and Bloodlust back to full. It does not stop Depth Charge picking the fight, so hold R for the chain, never for chip.

edits.before: Once you hit 6 and your first crit item, R Undying Rage neutralises his entire CC chain — bait the hook, survive, and kill him — and from there you scale away from a support-item tank who can't duel you.
edits.after: Undying Rage survives his CC chain but does not stop it — bait the hook, ride out Depth Charge, then kill him. From two items on you scale past a tank who cannot duel you, so take the fights he has not started.

notes: Followed the mirror's chart rather than the packet's (packet had Tryndamere, Skill, Skill, Nautilus, Tryndamere x3). Not written into prose but worth the user knowing: Dredge Line colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus to that terrain, so he can re-position onto your escape path and Tryndamere has no dash out of it — Flash is for the reposition, not the damage. Kit flag misfire, unchanged in both directions: tryndamere.json tags Mocking Shout (W) 'projectile', but Riot's text is a point-blank insulting cry, so no claim was made about it being blockable.
